1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and spacing between elements, as seen on the step 01 card, though letter spacing is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: No instruction text uses italics or all-caps and the longest paragraph is three sentences (regenerate page); the dense monospace Logs panel is a simulation diagnostic, not an instruction.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow centred column with large text and full-width buttons, which maps cleanly onto a mobile-width viewport.

4.why: Instructions are one to three short sentences in plain language, with only occasional jargon such as 'Provisioning information' and 'permanently consumed'.

5.why: Some fields show format examples via placeholders ('ABCD-1234-EF56-7890', '6 digits', 'marcus@example.com'), but the identity code field (step 02) and the authenticator code field (step 07) show no example at all.

6.why: No step gates progress behind a long text block; the longest required reading is the three-sentence regeneration warning.

7.why: The secret and recovery codes render as plain selectable text that can be copied, but no copy button is provided and the 'Manual secret entry' field still invites typing by hand.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent visual provisioning artifact appears anywhere; the provisioning screen shows only the text secret even though the copy mentions 'scanning a code'.

9.why: Nothing observable indicates one-time-code autofill or password-manager integration, though the plain email/phone fields would attract ordinary browser autofill heuristics.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading and a high-contrast blue primary button, but step 04 shows two equally prominent blue buttons ('Create authenticator setup' and 'Confirm authenticator'), diluting the primary action.

11.why: Several screens present multiple prominent actions at once, e.g. step 04 (create setup plus confirm) and the MFA settings hub with four full-width buttons.

12.why: Status lines such as 'Authenticator verification succeeded.' and 'Challenge ready. Enter the test code from Logs.' state what happened, but most messages omit what comes next and the error case gives no guidance.

13.why: 'Start over', 'Back to settings', repeatable challenge requests and code regeneration are all available without penalty, and codes are never masked, though no reveal/hide toggle exists.

14.why: The only observed error, 'The request could not be completed.', neither identifies the problem nor the fix, even though it avoids blaming language.

15.why: No countdown, timeout or expiry warning appears on any screen and the simulated test codes stayed valid throughout the session, though a live TOTP deployment would inherently impose a short code-entry window.
